title: Oblique-load lug fitting: margin of safety with the fitting factor and the lug interaction curve
who: Airframe stress engineers signing off fittings (wing-to-fuselage, landing gear, control-surface hinges)
why_hard: Each load component looks fine on its own (axial MS +0.92, transverse MS +0.26). Only the oblique-load interaction Ra^1.6 + Rtr^1.6 = 1 (Bruhn D1.8) shows the lug fails (MS -0.025). The fitting factor (14 CFR 25.625) sits on top of the 1.5 factor of safety. A model that checks the components separately, uses a linear or quadratic interaction, or drops the fitting factor signs off a failing part.
failure_cost: An unconservative fitting margin is a structural-substantiation error: found in certification review at best, in a test failure or an airworthiness directive at worst.
sources: Bruhn, Analysis and Design of Flight Vehicle Structures (1973), Section D1.8 (lugs under oblique load, interaction exponent 1.6)
